title: 256. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Interpreting Intercepts in Context
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Interpreting the \(y\)-Intercept of a Linear Cost Model
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the \(y\)-intercept of a linear cost function in a real-world context.
questions.question: A phone plan costs \(C=20+0.10m\) dollars, where \(m\) is the number of minutes used. What does the \(y\)-intercept \(20\) represent in this context?

options.label: B
options.text: The monthly fee when no minutes are used

questions.explanation: The \(y\)-intercept is the value of \(C\) when \(m=0\). Substituting \(m=0\) gives \(C=20+0.10(0)=20\). Thus the \(y\)-intercept represents the fixed monthly fee when no minutes are used. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: The \(y\)-intercept occurs when the input variable is zero.

questions.concept: Interpreting the \(x\)-Intercept of a Linear Model
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the \(x\)-intercept of a linear model as the time when a quantity reaches zero.
questions.question: A water tank has volume \(V=500-20t\) liters after \(t\) minutes. What does the \(x\)-intercept represent in this context?

options.label: B
options.text: The time until the tank is empty

questions.explanation: The \(x\)-intercept occurs when \(V=0\). Solving \(500-20t=0\) gives \(t=25\). This means the tank is empty after \(25\) minutes. Therefore the \(x\)-intercept represents the time until the tank is empty, so option B is correct.
questions.hint: The \(x\)-intercept occurs when the output value is zero.

questions.concept: Interpreting the \(y\)-Intercept of a Distance Model
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the \(y\)-intercept of a linear distance function as an initial distance.
questions.question: A cyclist's distance from home is \(d=15+20t\) kilometers after \(t\) hours. What does the \(y\)-intercept \(15\) represent?
questions.explanation: The \(y\)-intercept is the value of \(d\) when \(t=0\). Substituting \(t=0\) gives \(d=15+20(0)=15\). Thus the cyclist starts \(15\) kilometers from home. Therefore option B is correct.

questions.concept: Finding the \(x\)-Intercept of a Linear Model
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the \(x\)-intercept of a linear model and relate it to the context.
questions.question: A candle has length \(L=30-5t\) centimeters after \(t\) hours. What is the \(x\)-intercept, and what does it represent?

options.label: A
options.text: \(30\) hours; the initial length of the candle

options.label: B
options.text: \(6\) hours; the time until the candle burns out

questions.explanation: The \(x\)-intercept occurs when \(L=0\). Solving \(30-5t=0\) gives \(5t=30\), so \(t=6\). This means the candle burns out after \(6\) hours. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Set the output equal to zero and solve for the input.

questions.concept: Interpreting the \(x\)-Intercept of a Decreasing Linear Model
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the \(x\)-intercept of a decreasing linear function in context.
questions.question: The amount of water in a container is modeled by \(y=-3x+12\), where \(y\) is liters and \(x\) is minutes. Which statement correctly interprets the \(x\)-intercept?

options.label: A
options.text: It represents the time when the amount of water reaches zero.

options.label: B
options.text: It represents the initial amount of water.

questions.explanation: The \(x\)-intercept occurs when \(y=0\). Solving \(-3x+12=0\) gives \(x=4\). This means the container is empty after \(4\) minutes. Therefore the \(x\)-intercept represents the time when the water reaches zero, so option A is correct.
questions.hint: The \(x\)-intercept is found by setting the output equal to zero.

questions.concept: Interpreting the \(y\)-Intercept of a Membership Cost Model
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the \(y\)-intercept of a linear cost function as a one-time fixed fee.
questions.question: A gym membership costs \(C=50+25m\) dollars for \(m\) months. What does the \(y\)-intercept \(50\) represent?
questions.explanation: The \(y\)-intercept is the cost when \(m=0\). Substituting \(m=0\) gives \(C=50+25(0)=50\). This means there is a fixed cost of \(50\text{ dollars}\) even before any monthly fees are added. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: The \(y\)-intercept occurs when the number of months is zero.

questions.concept: Identifying the Relevant Intercept in Context
questions.learningObjective: Determine which intercept represents an initial amount in a real-world graph.
questions.question: A graph models the amount of water in a draining tank. It crosses the \(y\)-axis at \((0,8)\) and the \(x\)-axis at \((4,0)\). Which intercept represents the initial amount of water?
questions.explanation: The initial amount occurs at time \(x=0\). The point with \(x=0\) is \((0,8)\), so the \(y\)-intercept represents the initial amount of water. The point \((4,0)\) represents the time when the tank is empty. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: The initial value occurs when the input variable is zero.

questions.concept: Interpreting the \(y\)-Intercept of a Linear Model
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the \(y\)-intercept of a linear function as an initial value.
questions.question: The number of pages left to read is \(y=40-5x\) after \(x\) days. What does the \(y\)-intercept \(40\) represent?

options.label: B
options.text: The number of pages read per day

questions.explanation: The \(y\)-intercept is the value of \(y\) when \(x=0\). Substituting \(x=0\) gives \(y=40-5(0)=40\). This means there are \(40\) pages left at the start. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: The \(y\)-intercept gives the value of the output when the input is zero.

questions.concept: Choosing the Intercept That Represents Starting Distance
questions.learningObjective: Interpret intercepts from a graph in a distance context.
questions.question: A line passes through \((0,5)\) and \((10,0)\), where \(y\) is distance from a destination in kilometers and \(x\) is time in hours. Which intercept represents the starting distance from the destination?
questions.explanation: The starting distance occurs at time \(x=0\). The point with \(x=0\) is \((0,5)\), so the \(y\)-intercept represents the starting distance from the destination. The point \((10,0)\) represents the time when the destination is reached. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Look for the point where the input variable is zero.

questions.concept: Interpreting the \(x\)-Intercept as a Break-Even Point
questions.learningObjective: Interpret the \(x\)-intercept of a profit model as the break-even number of items.
questions.question: A company's profit is \(P=-200+40n\) dollars, where \(n\) is the number of items sold. What does the \(x\)-intercept represent in this context?

options.label: A
options.text: The profit when no items are sold

options.label: B
options.text: The break-even number of items sold

questions.explanation: The \(x\)-intercept occurs when \(P=0\). Solving \(-200+40n=0\) gives \(40n=200\), so \(n=5\). This means the company breaks even after selling \(5\) items. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Set the profit equal to zero and solve for the number of items.
